PAR-0436.title: Planet atmosphere rim drawn on the dark side too (Java glows only on the lit side)

notes.text: Headless pass could not reproduce or verify this visually (no Java leg/screenshots allowed). Code audit: client/shaders/atmosphere.gdshader is a near line-for-line port of core/assets/shaders/atmosphere.frag (same rayIntersection/inScatter/miePhase), and PlanetView.build_atmosphere/refresh_light pass the same uniforms as Shaders.AtmosphereShader.apply. Port-specific code is only the gamma-space additive composite (cdccec90) and render_mode depth_test_disabled/cull_back. Two leads for the Java pair: (1) Java's AtmosphereShader uses planet.getLightNormal() (world-frame, unrotated) while the port reuses the body's rotated mesh-frame light_dir - verify on a frame where getRotation() != 0; (2) Java depth-tests the atmosphere with depthMask(false), the port disables the depth test and relies on render_priority, so confirm which hemisphere survives. The fix, if needed, is in client/shaders/atmosphere.gdshader (outside this packet's ownership).

Code audit against the Java sources (no visual leg; nothing landed). (1) atmosphere.gdshader is line-for-line atmosphere.frag (rayIntersection/miePhase/rayleighPhase/density/optic/inScatter identical); port-only code is the gamma-space composite and 'depth_test_disabled, depth_draw_never'. (2) depthMask(false) is NOT the cause: Java Planet.drawAtmosphere sets Gl.depthMask(false) with the depth test on, the port disables the test and draws the additive sphere after the opaque body, so nothing writes depth in either path. (3) Light frame is the live lead: Java AtmosphereShader.apply sets u_light = planet.getLightNormal() = normalize(solarSystem.position - position), i.e. the UNROTATED world-frame sun, while Java's body (HexMesh.preRender) sets lightDir = same vector .rotate(Vec3.Y, getRotation()). The port passes the BODY's rotated mesh-frame planet_light.light_dir to both the body (planet.rs:1140) and the atmosphere (planet.rs:1148, 986), so its rim tracks the body's lit hemisphere instead of Java's world sun; they differ whenever getRotation() != 0. (4) Why this matters for 'rim on the dark side': night-side suppression in atmosphere.frag comes ONLY from exp(-n*(PEAK*color+FLARE)) in inScatter, where n is the optical depth of the outer-sphere ray toward l; rayleighPhase(0.75*(1+cc)) never reaches zero, so a light vector in the wrong frame (vs u_rcampos/u_campos, set from the planet-scene camera at planet.rs:1110-1112) leaves the geometric attenuation evaluating the wrong hemisphere and the shell glows all round. (5) Fix shape if the frame call is 'mesh frame': keep light_dir for the atmosphere but either rotate the shader's eye/dir into the world frame or feed getLightNormal unrotated and convert the camera uniforms; it is a uniform/frame decision that needs a Java+Godot frame pair at getRotation()!=0 (compare rim azimuth against the body terminator), so it was not landed blind. Shader file is in this packet's ownership for the follow-up.

PAR-0452.title: Sector shield gate is inverted: the three megabase sectors 246/244/242 are locked forever and Stormrider (27) is landable without them
PAR-0452.evidence: Java Sector.isShielded() asks whether the *preset's* shield list has an uncaptured sector: 'return preset != null && preset.shieldSectors.size > 0 && !isCaptured() && preset.shieldSectors.contains(s -> !s.isCaptured());'. SectorSubmissions.java:82 gives sector 27 the list [246,244,242], so 27 is shielded while any of the three megabases is uncaptured, and stops being shielded once all three are captured. SectorPreset.init sets the *reverse* visual link on the providers only: 'for(var other : shieldSectors){ other.shieldTarget = sector; }' (used by PlanetDialog.java:519 to draw the arc). The Rust port reuses that reverse link as the gate: 'pub fn is_shielded(&self) -> bool { self.shield_target.is_some() && !self.is_captured(None) }', and registries/sectors.rs link() writes 'sector.shield_target = Some(target)' onto 246/244/242. Result is exactly inverted: 246/244/242 report is_shielded() forever (they have shield_target and can never be captured, so !is_captured stays true) and sector 27 never reports it. The gate is live: ui/campaign.rs:1310 'let base_gate = def.generator != GeneratorKind::None && !sector.is_shielded();' sets view.selectable=false, and :939 'shielded: sector.is_shielded()'. Player-visible: the three endgame megabase sectors are permanently unselectable, and Stormrider can be launched without capturing them (Java's PlanetDialog.java:424 'if(sector.isShielded()) return false;').

Also assert mind-core::ui::campaign's sector view for 246 has selectable==true once captured and 27 shielded==true beforehand (existing sector-view test helpers).

PAR-0456.title: Autosave fires 60x too often: saveinterval is minutes in Java (time > saveinterval*60 s), seconds in the Rust port
PAR-0456.evidence: Java Saves.update accrues time in SECONDS (Time.delta) and compares against saveinterval*60: 'time += Time.delta; ... if(time > Core.settings.getInt("saveinterval") * 60 && !Vars.disableSave)' (Saves.java:216-219), so with the default saveinterval=60 (SettingsMenuDialog.java:373) the autosave is one hour apart. The Rust update_policy accrues seconds too ('self.time += update.delta_ticks as f32 / 60.0') but then compares against the raw setting: 'let interval = save_interval_seconds.max(0) as f32; if self.time > interval' (saves.rs:257-260), so the default writes an autosave every 60 s - 60x more frequent. The in-tree test update_policy_interval_is_seconds (saves.rs:708-742) encodes the wrong reading with the comment 'Saves.java:219 time > saveinterval * 60 in ticks'; Java's  is seconds, not ticks, and the multiply is the minutes->seconds conversion.

Rust EditorGrid::resize_shift does 'let nx = x + shift_x; let ny = y + shift_y;' (grid.rs:363-364) with no centring term, so old(px) -> new(px + shiftX). Effect: grow 100x100 -> 200x200 with shift 0 keeps the whole map in the bottom-left quadrant of the new map (all new space added top/right) where Java centres it at 50..149; shrink 200 -> 100 then crops only the top/right instead of all four sides, silently deleting a different part of the map. The ported unit test editor::lifecycle::resize_shift_preserves_tiles_and_data (lifecycle.rs:199-215) bakes in the wrong mapping: it expects (3,3)->(2,2) for 8x8->6x6 shift -1 where Java yields offsetX=(8-6)/2-(-1)=2, px=2+x, so old (3,3) lands on new (1,1).

boot-and-identity.title: Editor bridge → game scene → runtime connected → pid stamp
boot-and-identity.when: Start of any MCP session; after an editor, game, or branch/worktree change.
pre: Godot editor running with the open_godot_mcp addon bridge up.
No other editor holds this loop's bridge port (PARITY_BRIDGE_PORT, default 6970).
open-godot-mcp needs no DISPLAY on the opencode side; the editor needs a display (the loop wrapper provides the weston/Wayland GPU compositor, Xvfb is the software fallback).
success: `bridge_connected` + `runtime_connected` true.
Pid stable; `project` = expected checkout.
`tick` grows playing; `checksum` 16 hex.

steps: `godot_health {"action":"check"}`; require `bridge_connected: true`; down -> launch editor via `.opencode/loops/bin/run-godot-editor.sh` (loop or plain session; starts loop weston GPU compositor), wait ~20 s, retry.
`godot_editor_read {"action":"state"}`; `project_path` must contain `mindustry-godot`; loop: the loop's worktree, not a sibling checkout.
`godot_editor_edit {"action":"open_scene","params":{"path":"res://scenes/game.tscn"}}`.
`godot_game {"action":"play","params":{"scene":"res://scenes/game.tscn"}}`.
`godot_game {"action":"status"}`; require `runtime_connected: true`.

Pid stamp: `godot_exec {"action":"eval","params":{"code":"return {\"pid\": OS.get_process_id(), \"project\": ProjectSettings.globalize_path(\"res://\"), \"tick\": get_node(\"/root/Spine/SimHost\").get_tick(), \"checksum\": str(get_node(\"/root/Spine/SimHost\").get_checksum())}"}}`; save pid; re-stamp when it may change.

seed-survey.title: Seed sweep — boot both clients, enumerate a surface, one ledger item per element, classify with one action pair
seed-survey.when: The ledger needs seeding or extension from live surface: seeding.last_sweep is null, a run revealed a fork with no items, or the operator asks for a seed sweep.
pre: Both clients launchable on display :10 (java-reference-leg launch steps; boot-and-identity Godot steps).
Java window normalized to 1152x648; the Godot game is the embedded 1152x648 viewport.
TWIN-VERIFICATION.json readable; note the next PAR-#### id and the current item queue.
One surface (or one depth level) per sweep — do not chase the whole tree in one run.
success: One frame pair per classified element + surface pair, non-blank; `seed/diff-NN.json` metrics in the item.
Every element item has `path`/`parent`/`discovered_by`; matches `verified.mode: "seed"`; divergences `mismatch` + both frames + both legs' calls.
`seeding.last_sweep` updated; frontier = only unswept forks; clients at a known state (or stopped).
steps:
Create sweep run + launch both legs: `java-reference-leg` §Steps 1–3 (detached launch, readiness, unmaximize/resize/raise/capture) + `boot-and-identity` §Steps 1–6 (bridge, identity, `game.tscn`, play, pid); stamp both pids in `$RUN/run.json` + normalized Java geometry:
`RUN="runs/$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)-seed-<area>"`
`mkdir -p "$RUN/seed"`

Capture root/surface pair + gate (surface-render check; closes the surface item, e.g. PAR-0001 boot):
`capture_screen.py --window-title Mindustry --output "$RUN/seed/step-01-<surface>-java.png"`
`godot_screenshot {"action":"game"}    # copy the returned file to "$RUN/seed/step-01-<surface>-godot.png"`
`frame_diff.py --java "$RUN/seed/step-01-<surface>-java.png" --godot "$RUN/seed/step-01-<surface>-godot.png" --out-json "$RUN/seed/diff-01.json"`

Java: the capture IS the enumeration — read the image, list labels/rows/icons with capture-relative center; click = capture `region` origin + image offset; no OCR; hover probe (move, capture, diff) for unplaceable controls; re-measure after resize; never reuse older-run coords. Godot: one loop-free eval, centers in viewport coords (swap class for `Range`, `LineEdit`, ...); match by label + semantics; one-side-only element = finding, not rounding error:
`godot_exec {"action":"eval","params":{"code":"var root = get_node(\"/root/Spine/Ui/UiRoot\")\nvar rows = root.find_children(\"*\", \"Button\", true, false).filter(func(b): return b.is_visible_in_tree()).map(func(b): return {\"path\": str(b.get_path()), \"text\": str((b as BaseButton).text), \"center\": (b as Control).get_global_rect().get_center()})\nreturn {\"pid\": OS.get_process_id(), \"buttons\": rows}"}}`

One ledger item per element/action before classifying: `id` (next `PAR-####`), `title`, `surface`, `parent` (fork item, `null` at root), `status: "seeded"`, `chain` (`chains/<area>-<element>.md`), `discovered_by` = run dir, `path` = boot replay (exact calls, `java` then `godot`) + `path.confirm` (how the fork proves itself). In-game actions (move, shoot, mine, place, drag, rotate, select, pause, skip wave) are items too: `path` ends at a deterministic world (e.g. `ground-zero-fresh-launch`), `steps` carry the input.

Classify each with one action pair (stop at the first dialog/menu; no deeper chaining). Java (raise first): menu buttons may consume the first click as hover -> verify in the capture, second click same point before concluding a miss. Godot (center from step-3 listing; one discrete call per event, then flush). Gate per parity-eval skill §4: pass -> `status: verified`, `verified: {mode: "seed", date, run}`; fail -> `status: "mismatch"` + step, both frames, diff JSON, both legs' calls; fix flow reproduces the recorded stop once, then fixes; the sweep never edits code:
`window_ctl.py raise Mindustry`
`java_input.py move X Y`
`java_input.py click X Y left`
`capture_screen.py --window-title Mindustry --output "$RUN/seed/step-NN-<element>-java.png"`
`godot_input {"action":"mouse_motion","params":{"position":{"x":X,"y":Y},"coords":"viewport"}}`
`godot_input {"action":"mouse_button","params":{"button":"MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT","position":{"x":X,"y":Y},"coords":"viewport","pressed":true}}`
`godot_input {"action":"mouse_button","params":{"button":"MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT","position":{"x":X,"y":Y},"coords":"viewport","pressed":false}}`
`godot_exec {"action":"eval","params":{"code":"Input.flush_buffered_events()\nvar h = get_tree().root.gui_get_hovered_control()\nreturn {\"pid\": OS.get_process_id(), \"hovered\": (\"\" if h == null else str(h.get_path()))}"}}`
`godot_screenshot {"action":"game"}    # copy to "$RUN/seed/step-NN-<element>-godot.png"`
`frame_diff.py --java "$RUN/seed/step-NN-<element>-java.png" --godot "$RUN/seed/step-NN-<element>-godot.png" --out-json "$RUN/seed/diff-NN.json"`

Return both clients to the fork before the next element + confirm: Java `java_input.py keydown escape` + `java_input.py keyup escape` (split calls; each action re-activates the window) or Back/cancel; Godot `godot_input`/close. Re-capture/re-list, assert unchanged. Destructive entries (Quit, Abandon): classify on the confirm dialog, then cancel — never complete them.

Fork children: a new surface (Play → submenu; Campaign → planet page; sector → HUD) -> append to `seeding.frontier`; write controls as items whose `path` extends the current one with that action's calls; don't classify children this sweep; one depth level allowed -> descend once + repeat steps 2–6.

ui-control-click.title: Click a runtime-created UI Control and verify pressed via read-back (menu Play, paused Settings)
ui-control-click.when: Verifying that an injected mouse press reaches a runtime-created (ownerless) STOP-filter Button — menu buttons, dialog action buttons — instead of being swallowed by MindInput world input (EV-0062 class).
pre: boot-and-identity completed (editor bridge, res://scenes/game.tscn played with the explicit scene param, runtime_connected true, pid stamped).
Menu flow: the standalone menu is visible at boot (MenuGroup.visible true); wait for the boot fade (OverlayLayer/fade_in) to hide before clicking.
success: `pressed` increments on the `owner == null` Button; hovered path == resolved path before press.
Menu Play: `submenu_visible` true, 5 children; `dialog_stack` empty.
Paused Settings: `dialog_stack == ["paused", "settings"]`; settings visible, paused hidden.
`frames` advanced each read-back; `godot_log errors` empty.

steps:
Clear log; pid baseline; `Engine.get_process_frames()` must advance between calls:
`godot_log {"action":"clear"}`
`godot_exec {"action":"eval","params":{"code":"var ui_root = get_node(\"/root/Spine/Ui/UiRoot\")\nvar fade = ui_root.get_node_or_null(\"OverlayLayer/fade_in\")\nreturn {\"pid\": OS.get_process_id(), \"frames\": Engine.get_process_frames(), \"menu_visible\": ui_root.get_node(\"MenuGroup\").visible, \"fade_visible\": (fade != null and fade.visible)}"}}`

Paused leg: hide menu, Escape, `find_child` Settings — never assume a path (`.../paused/Center/Panel/Layout/Buttons/settings`, not `.../paused/settings`):
`godot_exec {"action":"call","params":{"node_path":"/root/Spine/Ui/UiRoot","method":"set_menu_visible","args":[false]}}`
`godot_input {"action":"key","params":{"key":"Escape","pressed":true}}`
`godot_input {"action":"key","params":{"key":"Escape","pressed":false}}`
`godot_exec {"action":"eval","params":{"code":"Input.flush_buffered_events()\nvar paused = get_node(\"/root/Spine/Ui/UiRoot/DialogLayer/paused\")\nvar s = paused.find_child(\"settings\", true, false)\nvar c = (s as Control).get_global_rect().get_center()\nreturn {\"pid\": OS.get_process_id(), \"path\": str(s.get_path()), \"owned\": s.owner != null, \"center\": {\"x\": int(c.x), \"y\": int(c.y)}, \"stack\": str(get_node(\"/root/MindUi\").call(\"dialog_stack\"))}"}}`

Click the resolved center (`coords: "viewport"`); one discrete call per event, never batch a pair:
`godot_input {"action":"mouse_motion","params":{"position":{"x":CX,"y":CY},"coords":"viewport"}}`
`godot_input {"action":"mouse_button","params":{"button":"MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT","position":{"x":CX,"y":CY},"coords":"viewport","pressed":true}}`
`godot_input {"action":"mouse_button","params":{"button":"MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT","position":{"x":CX,"y":CY},"coords":"viewport","pressed":false}}`
